title: AS2 compiler: class extends uses ActionNewObject instead of ActionExtends (0x69) — calls super constructor during prototype setup
description:
In compileClassDecl(), when a class has a superClass, the compiler emits:
  push 0 (nArgs), push superName, ActionNewObject (0x40) → assigns to ClassName.prototype

This is WRONG. ActionNewObject CALLS the superclass constructor with 0 args, causing side effects (e.g. throws if constructor requires args, initializes unintended state).

The correct AVM1 opcode is ActionExtends (0x69), which creates a properly linked prototype object WITHOUT calling the constructor. Ruffle's action_extends() (activation.rs:1054):
  - pops: superclass, then subclass
  - creates a new sub_prototype whose __proto__ is superclass.prototype
  - sets sub_prototype.__constructor__ = superclass (this is the CRITICAL link — used by super() to find the right superclass constructor)
  - sets subclass.prototype = sub_prototype

The current new SuperClass() approach also MISSES setting __constructor__, which breaks:
  - Ruffle's super() handling that resolves via __proto__.__constructor__
  - instanceof checks that walk the prototype chain via __constructor__

Fix in packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts compileClassDecl():
  Replace the 'Emit prototype chain if extends' block with:
    push className, ActionGetVariable (subclass)
    push superName, ActionGetVariable (superclass)
    emit 0x69 (ActionExtends)
  Remove the ActionNewObject-based prototype assignment and the manual constructor= restoration (ActionExtends handles __constructor__ automatically).

References:
  - ruffle/core/src/avm1/activation.rs fn action_extends() (line 1054)
  - ruffle/swf/src/avm1/opcode.rs: Extends = 0x69
